method: Input is read in the browser. A leading 'errno' with an optional colon or hash is stripped, then a run of digits with an optional sign is decoded as a number: the sign is ignored, 0 is reported as success, 41 and 58 are reported as the two unassigned numbers in the 1 to 133 range, and anything outside that range is refused with the range in the message. Any other input is matched case-insensitively against the symbols: an optional E prefix is accepted, so acces or eacces both reach EACCES, and the three alias symbols EWOULDBLOCK, EDEADLOCK and ENOTSUP resolve to 11, 35 and 95 and are named back as aliases. Numbers, symbols and the default message text come from the kernel's asm-generic/errno.h numbering as glibc's strerror renders it: 131 assigned values from 1 EPERM to 133 EHWPOISON. Each entry carries one of eleven categories (permission, files, resources, processes, arguments, I/O, sockets, locks, keys, programs and historical System V/STREAMS values), and 24 common errors carry a short what-to-check note. The reference list below the form shows all 131 entries, filters on number, symbol, message, category or alias, and every row can be decoded with a click or keyboard press. The page executes nothing, stores nothing and makes no network request; the table is a fixed snapshot and does not vary with the reader's kernel.

sources.title: errno(3) — a failing call sets a positive errno number, a successful call never clears it, and each thread has its own copy
asm-generic/errno.h — the kernel's generic error numbers 1 to 133, with 41 and 58 unassigned
strerror(3) — renders an error number as the message text this page shows
